category_title: Active and vocal students during teacher-led instruction
minimal_context: The student is working on a computer using the Novanet online instructional program for self-paced learning.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please get on your computers and start your self-paced learning on the Novanet program.

STUDENT: Do we have to use Novanet? I strongly feel that this program is boring.

TUTOR: Please just log in and start working on your assignment.

STUDENT: I'm just clicking through it. I do not seem to learn from the online lessons at all.

TUTOR: Keep trying, you need to finish the module today.

STUDENT: I'm not doing this anymore. I'm completely discontent with this Novanet program, it's entirely boring and I refuse to use it!

options.A: Require the student to use a note-taking application on the computer to organize their work and archive past Novanet modules.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines and strict deadlines for the student to complete their self-paced Novanet modules.
options.C: Utilize differentiated instruction, including guided practice, direct teaching, one-on-one instruction, role play, games, group learning, peer tutoring, and a whatever-works approach.
options.D: Provide the student with an endless supply of self-paced Novanet problems to work on during the session.
